1	# D4D Rubric10 - Ten-Element Hierarchical Evaluation Rubric
2	# Schema Version: 2.1
3	# Last Updated: 2026-01-12
4	
5	# =============================================================================
6	# FIELD REFERENCE GUIDE
7	# =============================================================================
8	# Use these exact field names when evaluating D4D files against the schema.
9	# The D4D schema uses a class-based structure, not dot-notation.
10	#
11	# Discovery & Access:
12	#   - id: Unique identifier (URI)
13	#   - doi: Digital Object Identifier
14	#   - rrid: Research Resource Identifier
15	#   - title: Dataset title
16	#   - description: Dataset description
17	#   - keywords: Search keywords (list)
18	#   - download_url: Download URL
19	#   - page: Landing page URL
20	#   - distribution_formats: DistributionFormat (list)
21	#
22	# Licensing & Governance:
23	#   - license_and_use_terms: LicenseAndUseTerms class
24	#   - ip_restrictions: IPRestrictions class
25	#   - regulatory_restrictions: ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions class
26	#   - confidentiality_level: ConfidentialityLevelEnum
27	#
28	# Human Subjects:
29	#   - human_subject_research: HumanSubjectResearch class
30	#   - informed_consent: InformedConsent (list)
31	#   - participant_privacy: ParticipantPrivacy (list)
32	#   - participant_compensation: HumanSubjectCompensation class
33	#   - vulnerable_populations: VulnerablePopulations class
34	#   - ethical_reviews: EthicalReview (list)
35	#
36	# Data Composition:
37	#   - instances: Instance (list)
38	#   - variables: VariableMetadata (list)
39	#   - subpopulations: Subpopulation (list)
40	#   - is_tabular: Boolean
41	#   - is_deidentified: Deidentification class
42	#
43	# Data Quality:
44	#   - anomalies: DataAnomaly (list)
45	#   - known_biases: DatasetBias (list)
46	#   - known_limitations: DatasetLimitation (list)
47	#
48	# Use Guidance:
49	#   - intended_uses: IntendedUse (list)
50	#   - prohibited_uses: ProhibitedUse (list)
51	#   - discouraged_uses: DiscouragedUse (list)
52	#   - existing_uses: ExistingUse (list)
53	#
54	# Hierarchical Structure:
55	#   - resources: Dataset (list) - nested sub-resources
56	#   - parent_datasets: Dataset (list) - parent datasets
57	#   - related_datasets: DatasetRelationship (list) - typed relationships
58	#
59	# Funding & Motivation:
60	#   - purposes: Purpose (list)
61	#   - tasks: Task (list)
62	#   - funders: FundingMechanism (list)
63	#   - creators: Creator (list)
64	#
65	# Technical Methods:
66	#   - collection_mechanisms: CollectionMechanism (list)
67	#   - acquisition_methods: DataAcquisition (list)
68	#   - preprocessing_strategies: PreprocessingStrategy (list)
69	#   - cleaning_strategies: CleaningStrategy (list)
70	#   - labeling_strategies: LabelingStrategy (list)
71	#   - software_and_tools: Software (list)
72	#
73	# Versioning & Maintenance:
74	#   - version: Version string
75	#   - version_access: VersionAccess class
76	#   - updates: UpdatePlan class
77	#   - errata: Erratum (list)
78	#   - maintainers: Maintainer (list)
79	#   - was_derived_from: Source provenance
80	#   - release_notes: Release documentation
81	#
82	# Distribution:
83	#   - format: File format specification
84	#   - media_type: MIME type
85	#   - encoding: Character encoding
86	#   - bytes: File size in bytes
87	#   - conforms_to: Standards conformance
88	#   - conforms_to_schema: Schema conformance
89	#
90	# Other:
91	#   - publisher: Publishing organization
92	#   - citation: Recommended citation
93	#   - external_resources: ExternalResource (list)
94	#   - sensitive_elements: Sensitive content description
95	#   - content_warnings: Content warnings
96	#
97	# Data Protection & Compliance:
98	#   - data_protection_impacts: DataProtectionImpact (list)
99	#   - reidentification_risk: Re-identification risk assessment
100	#   - hipaa_compliant: ComplianceStatusEnum
101	#   - other_compliance: Other regulatory frameworks (list)
102	#   - governance_committee_contact: Governance committee contact person
103	#
104	# Responsible AI (CROISSANT RAI Alignment):
105	#   - future_use_impacts: FutureUseImpact (rai:dataSocialImpact) - Social impact analysis
106	#   - intended_uses: IntendedUse (rai:dataUseCases) - Explicit intended uses
107	#   - known_biases: DatasetBias (rai:dataBiases) - Categorized with BiasTypeEnum
108	#
109	# Data Quality & Documentation:
110	#   - missing_data_documentation: MissingDataDocumentation (list)
111	#   - annotation_analyses: AnnotationAnalysis (list)
112	#   - machine_annotation_tools: MachineAnnotationTool (list)
113	#   - raw_data_sources: RawDataSource (list)
114	#   - imputation_protocols: ImputationProtocol (list)
115	#
116	# Dataset Structure Flags:
117	#   - is_data_split: Boolean - Training/test split flag
118	#   - is_subpopulation: Boolean - Subpopulation subset flag
119	#   - confidential_elements: Confidentiality (list)
120	#
121	# Provenance (W3C PROV-O):
122	#   - was_derived_from: Source provenance with entity-activity-agent relationships
123	#   - Note: Provenance may be represented as text OR as W3C PROV-O graphs
124	#
125	# AI/ML Readiness (Bridge2AI):
126	#   - Reference: Bridge2AI AI-readiness characterization criteria
127	#   - Tool: Bridge2AI AI-readiness scorecard
128	#
129	# Data Sustainability:
130	#   - Persistent identifiers (DOI, ARK, Handle)
131	#   - Long-term governance plan
132	#   - Domain-appropriate repository
133	#   - Institutional commitment documentation
134	#
135	# Integration/Merging Capability:
136	#   - Common identifiers for cross-dataset integration
137	#   - Standardized formats for data harmonization
138	#   - Integration procedure documentation
139	# =============================================================================

141	d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225	
226	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
227	    - id: 5
228	      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
229	      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
230	      sub_elements:
231	        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
232	          field: ["subpopulations"]
233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
236	          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
237	        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
240	          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242	
243	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]
269	        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
270	          field: ["funders"]
271	        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
272	          field: ["funders"]
273	        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
274	          field: ["creators", "funders"]
275	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
276	
277	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
278	    - id: 8
279	      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
280	      description: >
281	        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
289	          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
293	          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:
305	        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
308	          field: ["known_biases"]
309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
310	          field: ["anomalies"]
311	        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
312	          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
313	        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
314	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
315	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
316	
317	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
318	    - id: 10
319	      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
320	      description: >
321	        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
322	
323	        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
324	        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
325	        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
326	        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
327	      sub_elements:
328	        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
329	          field: ["publisher"]
330	        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
331	          field: ["citation", "doi"]
332	        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
333	          field: ["conforms_to"]
334	        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
335	          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
336	        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
337	          field: ["related_datasets"]
338	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
339

d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
  schema_version: "2.0"
  description: >
    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.

  scoring_scale:
    element: 0–5
    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass

  rubric:
    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 1
      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
          field: ["title", "description"]
        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
          field: ["keywords"]
        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
          field: ["page", "resources"]
        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 2
      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
          field: ["download_url"]
        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 3
      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
      description: >
        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
          field: ["format", "encoding"]
        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
          field: ["variables"]
        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 4
      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
          field: ["is_deidentified"]
        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
          field: ["informed_consent"]
        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 5
      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
          field: ["subpopulations"]
        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 6
      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
          field: ["version"]
        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
          field: ["version_access"]
        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
          field: ["errata", "updates"]
        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
          field: ["updates"]
        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 7
      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
          field: ["purposes"]
        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
          field: ["tasks"]
        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
          field: ["creators", "funders"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 8
      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
      description: >
        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
          field: ["software_and_tools"]
        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 9
      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
          field: ["known_limitations"]
        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
          field: ["known_biases"]
        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
          field: ["anomalies"]
        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 10
      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
      description: >
        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
          field: ["publisher"]
        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
          field: ["citation", "doi"]
        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
          field: ["conforms_to"]
        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
          field: ["related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

16	id: https://chorus4ai.org/
17	name: CHoRUS Dataset
18	title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'
19	description: >-
20	  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the
21	  Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded
22	  Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from
23	  intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a
24	  cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient
25	  admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized
26	  electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data;
27	  a September 2025 training webinar instead reported over 45,000 unique admissions across 14
28	  hospitals as of August 2025. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9
29	  data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60
30	  members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication
31	  administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing
32	  flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with
33	  the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and
34	  gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry
35	  sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only
36	  tokens shared. The project also states an intention to sequester a holdout test set for external
37	  validation of models.

39	  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
40	  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."

48	  clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema; imaging follows the DICOM schema; waveform
49	  telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema; waveform EEG follows the open-source

332	- source_description: Unstructured clinical notes held in hospital electronic health record systems
333	  source_type: Hospital electronic health record
334	  raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit
335	  access_details: Note text is stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are placed in the shared enclave.
336	- source_description: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS)
337	  source_type: Clinical imaging archive
338	  raw_data_format: DICOM
339	- source_description: Bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware
340	  source_type: Clinical monitoring device stream
341	  raw_data_format: Waveform telemetry converted to WFDB
342	- source_description: Hospital EEG databases

346	preprocessing_strategies:
347	- preprocessing_details: >-
348	    Standardization of structured EHR data to the OMOP Common Data Model, using validated semantic
349	    mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled
350	    tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository.
351	- preprocessing_details: >-
352	    Extraction and tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP
353	    toolkit.
354	- preprocessing_details: >-
355	    Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, including de-identification
356	    of imaging, which was in process for the larger imaging cohort as of August 2025.
357	- preprocessing_details: >-
358	    Conversion of waveform telemetry into WFDB using the waveform conversion scripts and preparation
359	    resources maintained for waveform release.
360	- preprocessing_details: >-
361	    Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using the open source UF-Geocoding code
362	    maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization.
363	
364	cleaning_strategies:
365	- cleaning_details: >-
366	    Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data
367	    submissions, and site status tracking is used to identify and resolve blocking issues in the
368	    creation and curation of a site's data extract.
369

371	- labeling_details: >-
372	    The project states that a visualization and annotation environment will label data with targets
373	    important for prediction, and that it will develop capabilities across the multi-center network
374	    to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize and label data.
375	  data_annotation_protocol: >-
376	    Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping and validation under a clinical validation
377	    SOP associated with the chorus-mapping repository.
378	  source_caveats: >-
379	    The annotation environment is described in the future tense in the award abstract and the GitHub
380	    organization overview; the bundle does not report labels present in the released data.
381	
382	machine_annotation_tools:
383	- tools:
384	  - OHNLP toolkit
385	  tool_descriptions: >-
386	    Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized automatically using the OHNLP toolkit, and the
387	    resulting tokens are published against the OHNLP open-source schema.
388	
389	missing_data_documentation:
390	- missing_data_patterns: >-
391	    Modality coverage was uneven at the August 2025 snapshot: OMOP data and telemetry were in the
392	    enclave, clinical notes were stored locally with only tokens shared, roughly 1,000 images were
393	    available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in
394	    process. Published metadata existed for demographics, medication administration, procedures,
395	    nursing flowsheets, diagnoses and waveform telemetry, while metadata for clinical notes, imaging
396	    and EEG was marked planned.
397	  missing_data_causes: >-
398	    De-identification, extraction and metadata publication workflows for imaging, EEG and clinical
399	    notes were still in progress.

401	is_deidentified:
402	  method: >-
403	    Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is
404	    tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit rather than shared as free text; imaging de-identification was
405	    in process as of August 2025.
406	  deidentification_details: >-
407	    Clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens placed in the shared
408	    enclave, so that identifiable narrative text is not distributed with the dataset.
409	  source_caveats: >-
410	    The bundle does not enumerate the identifiers removed, name a de-identification standard, or
411	    report residual re-identification risk. A privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid
412	    repository exist in the chorus-ai GitHub organization, but the bundle does not state that either
413	    was applied to the released data.

416	- sensitive_elements_present: true
417	  sensitivity_details: >-
418	    The dataset consists of hospital records of critically ill patients, including demographics,
419	    diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, imaging, physiologic
420	    waveforms, EEG and tokenized clinical notes.
421	- sensitive_elements_present: true

428	- confidential_elements_present: true

432	- confidential_elements_present: true

445	    Patient-focused work within the consortium determines the ethical and legal approaches used to

700	source_caveats: >-
701	  Four sources were used, ranked: the CHoRUS project website (project_documentation, tier 2), the
702	  NIH RePORTER project page for OT2OD032701 (tier 4), the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care
703	  Cohort 2 informational webinar of September 2025 (tier 4), and a 2025-11-14 capture of the
704	  chorus-ai GitHub organization overview (tier 5). The 2022 award abstract is written in the future
705	  tense about project plans and is recorded here as intention rather than as current dataset state.
706	  Volume figures differ between the tier-2 website (50,000 released admissions) and the tier-4
707	  webinar (over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025); the higher-ranked figure is stated with
708	  the disagreement noted at the affected instance. The webinar's imaging figure (1,000 images) and
709	  the website's (7,642 admissions with radiology data) count different units and are both retained.
710	  The 23 Tb waveform figure is reported for waveform data only, so no dataset-wide size is recorded.
711	  The cohort 2 webinar lists six people under the heading "Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team" with
712	  institutions but no individual role descriptions; only Eric Rosenthal is independently attested as

714	  person-valued field the Creator class declares, so it carries each listed leader. The bundle
715	  states that CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and collaborates with the
716	  other three, but names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded.

# D4D Datasheet for CHORUS Dataset
# Generation Method: schema-grounded agentic, phase 1
# Agent runtime: Claude API (direct)
# Provider: LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic)
# Model: claude-opus-5
# Mode: four-phase project agent, generic-v8 prompt
# Prompt: src/download/prompts/d4d_generic_arm_prompt_v8.md (identical for all projects)
# Arm: BASELINE (input documents only)
# Source bundle: data/preprocessed/concatenated/CHORUS_preprocessed.txt
# Source manifest: data/preprocessed/source_manifest.yaml
# Schema: src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema_all.yaml
# Prior D4D factual reuse: prohibited
# Temperature: 0.0
# Generated: 2026-09-07

id: https://chorus4ai.org/
name: CHoRUS Dataset
title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'
description: >-
  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the
  Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded
  Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from
  intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a
  cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient
  admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized
  electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data;
  a September 2025 training webinar instead reported over 45,000 unique admissions across 14
  hospitals as of August 2025. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9
  data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60
  members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication
  administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing
  flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with
  the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and
  gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry
  sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only
  tokens shared. The project also states an intention to sequester a holdout test set for external
  validation of models.
notes: >-
  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."
status: Partially released under controlled access; acquisition, de-identification and curation continuing under NIH award OT2OD032701, whose project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.
page: https://chorus4ai.org/
created_by: CHoRUS Consortium
conforms_to: >-
  Structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication administration, procedures,
  nursing flowsheets, diagnoses) are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with published
  OMOP-schema metadata and OMOP schema extensions for nursing flowsheets; extracted and tokenized
  clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema; imaging follows the DICOM schema; waveform
  telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema; waveform EEG follows the open-source
  EDF+ and Persyst schemas.
conforms_to_standard:
- OMOP_CDM
- DICOM
- WFDB
- OTHER
conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
conforms_to_class: Dataset
keywords:
- critical care
- acute illness
- intensive care unit
- electronic health records
- OMOP Common Data Model
- waveform telemetry
- electroencephalography
- medical imaging
- social determinants of health
- artificial intelligence
- machine learning
- Bridge2AI

purposes:
- response: >-
    To meet the need for generating data for machine learning and artificial intelligence
    applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications,
    and measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    To develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods used
    promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit.
- response: >-
    To provision a holdout test set accessible for external validation of models, aiding marketplace
    adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
- response: >-
    To create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and to create best
    practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the Bridge2AI consortium.
- response: >-
    To develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready dataset addressing the
    grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.

tasks:
- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
- response: Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    External validation of machine learning models against a sequestered holdout dataset.
- response: >-
    Labeling data with targets important for prediction, using a visualization and annotation
    environment.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
    learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center datasets is described as a
    critical first step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
- response: >-
    Existing resources lack a diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready critical care
    dataset able to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
- response: >-
    Multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data are not harmonized across centers; CHoRUS
    develops unified standards to harmonize them.
- response: >-
    Sequestered holdout data for independent external validation of clinical AI models are scarce,
    which the project addresses by sequestering holdout datasets.

instances:
- instance_type: Patient admission from an intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
  counts: 50000
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
  notes: >-
    Figure for the current released dataset. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient
    admissions.
  source_caveats: >-
    Sources disagree on admission volume. The project website (tier 2, documentation) reports 50,000
    admissions in the current released dataset; the cohort 2 informational webinar (tier 4)
    states that as of August 2025 the dataset covered 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique
    admissions. The higher-ranked project website value is stated here.
- instance_type: Row of OMOP-standardized electronic health record data
  counts: 1600000000
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:9
  notes: >-
    The website reports "1.6 Billion Rows of EHR OMOP data" for the current released dataset; the
    integer given here is this record's own expansion of that rounded figure, not a count reported
    exactly by any source.
- instance_type: Demographics record
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:6
  notes: Standardized to OMOP; metadata published against the OMOP schema.
- instance_type: Medication administration record, time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:8
  notes: Standardized to OMOP; metadata published against the OMOP schema.
- instance_type: Procedure documented by providers
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
  notes: Standardized to OMOP; metadata published against the OMOP schema.
- instance_type: Nursing flowsheet entry (high-frequency documentation)
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
  notes: Standardized to OMOP; metadata published against the OMOP schema with extensions.
- instance_type: Diagnosis documented by providers
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:7
  notes: Standardized to OMOP; metadata published against the OMOP schema.
- instance_type: Clinical note, extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:32
  notes: >-
    Notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are placed in the shared enclave.
    Published metadata follows the OHNLP open-source schema; as of August 2025 the metadata entry
    for this modality was marked planned.
- instance_type: Admission with radiology imaging data obtained from hospital PACS
  counts: 7642
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15
  notes: >-
    The project website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released
    dataset. Imaging follows the DICOM schema; metadata was marked planned as of August 2025.
  source_caveats: >-
    The two sources count different units and were both retained rather than reconciled: the project
    website (tier 2) reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the cohort 2 webinar
    (tier 4) states that as of August 2025 imaging was "currently 1000 images available with de-id
    in process for larger cohort".
- instance_type: Waveform telemetry recording from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
  notes: >-
    Stored in WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema. The project website reports 23 Tb of waveform
    data in the current released dataset.
- instance_type: Waveform EEG recording from hospital EEG databases
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
  notes: >-
    Stored as EDF+ and Persyst; extraction was in process as of August 2025 and the metadata entry
    was marked planned.

subpopulations:
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Released admissions are identified by care setting as adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric
    intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) admissions.
  source_caveats: The bundle does not report the distribution of admissions across these settings.

splits:
- split_details: >-
    The award abstract states that the dataset will also provision a holdout test set, accessible
    for model external validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models, and describes
    sequestering holdout datasets for external validation.
  source_caveats: >-
    Stated as a project intention in the 2022 award abstract; the bundle does not state the size,
    composition or availability of the holdout set.

acquisition_methods:
- acquisition_details: >-
    Retrospective collection: clinical data generated during routine care are extracted at
    contributing hospitals, standardized, tokenized, stored, visualized and labeled through a
    multi-center network, then delivered as a CHoRUS data extract to the shared cloud enclave.

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    Extraction of structured electronic health record data at contributing sites and standardization
    to the OMOP Common Data Model, supported by the OHDSI tool stack.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Extraction of clinical notes and tokenization using the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains at the
    site and only tokens are shared.
- mechanism_details: Retrieval of imaging studies from hospital PACS in DICOM form.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Capture of waveform telemetry from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware, converted to WFDB
    using the waveform conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository.
- mechanism_details: Extraction of EEG waveforms from hospital EEG databases as EDF+ and Persyst.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Site-side tooling for building and delivering submissions, including the chorus-extract-upload
    tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract and dockerized container applications deployed
    to support CHoRUS services on Azure.

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    Data collection is retrospective. As of August 2025 the assembled dataset covered 14 different
    hospitals. The funded project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not state the calendar range of the clinical encounters represented in the data;
    the dates given are the award project period and the August 2025 status snapshot.

data_collectors:
- collector_details: >-
    Fourteen data acquisition centers, drawn from a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers,
    contribute clinical data extracts. Site data managers follow the step-by-step extraction and
    contribution workflow documented in the Chorus_SOP repository and report progress through
    regular status updates.
  role: Data contributing sites
- collector_details: >-
    CHoRUS sub-teams for Standards, Data Acquisition and Tooling support extraction, mapping and
    delivery and maintain the recordings and documentation referenced from the workflow diagram.
  role: Consortium sub-teams

direct_collection:
- is_direct: false
  collection_details: >-
    Data are obtained retrospectively from hospital clinical systems - electronic health records,
    PACS, bedside monitor gateways and hospital EEG databases - at contributing centers, rather than
    collected directly from individuals for research purposes.

sampling_strategies:
- strategies: >-
    Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies,
    within a legal framework established for collecting data at scale. Federated access enabling
    sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort.
  notes: >-
    The project states an aim of assembling the most diverse dataset addressing recovery from acute
    illness; the bundle does not describe the sampling frame or selection criteria in operational
    detail.

raw_data_sources:
- source_description: Structured electronic health record systems at 14 data contributing hospitals
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record
  raw_data_format: Site-native EHR extracts mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model
- source_description: Unstructured clinical notes held in hospital electronic health record systems
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record
  raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit
  access_details: Note text is stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are placed in the shared enclave.
- source_description: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS)
  source_type: Clinical imaging archive
  raw_data_format: DICOM
- source_description: Bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware
  source_type: Clinical monitoring device stream
  raw_data_format: Waveform telemetry converted to WFDB
- source_description: Hospital EEG databases
  source_type: Clinical neurophysiology database
  raw_data_format: EDF+ and Persyst

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Standardization of structured EHR data to the OMOP Common Data Model, using validated semantic
    mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled
    tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Extraction and tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP
    toolkit.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, including de-identification
    of imaging, which was in process for the larger imaging cohort as of August 2025.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Conversion of waveform telemetry into WFDB using the waveform conversion scripts and preparation
    resources maintained for waveform release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using the open source UF-Geocoding code
    maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data
    submissions, and site status tracking is used to identify and resolve blocking issues in the
    creation and curation of a site's data extract.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    The project states that a visualization and annotation environment will label data with targets
    important for prediction, and that it will develop capabilities across the multi-center network
    to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize and label data.
  data_annotation_protocol: >-
    Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping and validation under a clinical validation
    SOP associated with the chorus-mapping repository.
  source_caveats: >-
    The annotation environment is described in the future tense in the award abstract and the GitHub
    organization overview; the bundle does not report labels present in the released data.

machine_annotation_tools:
- tools:
  - OHNLP toolkit
  tool_descriptions: >-
    Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized automatically using the OHNLP toolkit, and the
    resulting tokens are published against the OHNLP open-source schema.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Modality coverage was uneven at the August 2025 snapshot: OMOP data and telemetry were in the
    enclave, clinical notes were stored locally with only tokens shared, roughly 1,000 images were
    available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in
    process. Published metadata existed for demographics, medication administration, procedures,
    nursing flowsheets, diagnoses and waveform telemetry, while metadata for clinical notes, imaging
    and EEG was marked planned.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    De-identification, extraction and metadata publication workflows for imaging, EEG and clinical
    notes were still in progress.

is_deidentified:
  method: >-
    Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is
    tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit rather than shared as free text; imaging de-identification was
    in process as of August 2025.
  deidentification_details: >-
    Clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens placed in the shared
    enclave, so that identifiable narrative text is not distributed with the dataset.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not enumerate the identifiers removed, name a de-identification standard, or
    report residual re-identification risk. A privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid
    repository exist in the chorus-ai GitHub organization, but the bundle does not state that either
    was applied to the released data.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset consists of hospital records of critically ill patients, including demographics,
    diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, imaging, physiologic
    waveforms, EEG and tokenized clinical notes.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    Social determinants of health, which the unified standards are to harmonize, and contextual
    factors that the award abstract states data elements will feature, such as geographic distance
    to the nearest hospital.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: true
  confidentiality_details: >-
    Clinical note text is confidential to the contributing site: it is stored locally and is not
    placed in the shared enclave, which receives only tokens.
- confidential_elements_present: true
  confidentiality_details: >-
    Every documented modality is marked as controlled for access control; the dataset is not openly
    downloadable.

participant_privacy:
- anonymization_method: >-
    Tokenization of unstructured EHR text, de-identification of imaging, and transformation of data
    using approaches that limit re-identification.
  privacy_techniques: >-
    Local retention of clinical note text at contributing sites, with only tokens shared. Controlled
    access to all modalities within a cloud enclave.
  notes: >-
    Patient-focused work within the consortium determines the ethical and legal approaches used to
    manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  regulatory_compliance:
  - >-
    The project establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing
    legal and regulatory landscape as part of its ethics work.
  special_populations:
  - >-
    Released admissions include pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU)
    patients.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the
    dataset.

at_risk_populations:
  at_risk_groups_included: true
  source_caveats: >-
    Inclusion of minors follows from the released dataset covering PICU and NICU admissions; the
    bundle describes no assent procedures, guardian consent procedures or special protections.

ethical_reviews:
- review_details: >-
    The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate
    for public sharing.
  source_caveats: >-
    Described in the award abstract as project ethics activity; the bundle names no institutional
    review board, ethics committee or reviewing organization for the dataset.
- review_details: >-
    The consortium evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase
    trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI, developing new approaches as the existing legal
    and regulatory landscape is analyzed.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Imaging coverage was partial at the August 2025 snapshot, with roughly 1,000 images available
    and de-identification in process for a larger cohort.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    EEG data extraction was still in process as of August 2025, so EEG coverage of the released
    admissions was incomplete.
- limitation_type: integration_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are available in the
    shared enclave, so analyses requiring full note text cannot be performed on the shared data.
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Data come from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers and
    cover acute and critical care admissions only, so the population is not a general hospital or
    general population sample.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The released dataset of 50,000 admissions is smaller than the anticipated final dataset of
    100,000 patient admissions, and modality-level metadata publication was incomplete.
  scope_impact: >-
    Analyses run on the current release may not generalize to the completed dataset, whose
    composition across modalities is expected to change.
  source_caveats: >-
    The comparison between the released and anticipated admission counts is this record's own
    juxtaposition of the two figures the project website states (50,000 and 100,000); neither source
    states a completion fraction.

license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    Access to the dataset is controlled. Participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care
    Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before
    gaining access to the dataset.
  notes: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project is licensed under the MIT License,
    with individual repositories carrying MIT or Apache-2.0; this covers CHoRUS software and tooling
    rather than the clinical dataset.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle states the licensing agreement requirement only in the context of the training
    program registration flow and does not reproduce the agreement or name a data use license for
    the dataset itself.

data_governance:
  accountable_organization:
    name: Massachusetts General Hospital
  access_review_process: >-
    All modalities are under controlled access. Access requests are directed to named CHoRUS
    contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). For the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI
    for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email
    and institution and sign the licensing agreement included in that form; once access is granted
    and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. A ".edu" email address is
    required to gain access to the dataset, and program administrators assist with this access where
    needed.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle names access contacts but does not name a data access committee, its membership, an
    access decision timeframe, or an appeal process. Massachusetts General Hospital is recorded as
    accountable organization because it is the awardee organization for OT2OD032701 and hosts the
    program manager; the bundle does not use the term data steward.

regulatory_restrictions:
  confidentiality_level: restricted
  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
    All nine documented data types are marked as controlled for access control, and access requires
    a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (".edu") email address. Data are worked with
    inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not state HIPAA, GDPR or export-control determinations for the dataset; HIPAA
    and GDPR compliance appear only as topics of a training workshop on IRB, data compliance and
    quality assurance.

distribution_formats:
- format: OMOP Common Data Model relational tables
  notes: >-
    Demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets and diagnoses, with
    published metadata against the OMOP schema (with extensions for nursing flowsheets).
- format: OHNLP open-source schema (tokenized clinical notes)
  notes: >-
    Notes are extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains stored locally at
    contributing sites and only tokens are shared. Metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
- format: DICOM
  notes: Imaging obtained from PACS; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
- format: WFDB
  notes: Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware, documented against an extended PhysioNet schema.
- format: EDF+ and Persyst
  notes: Waveform EEG from hospital databases, documented against the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.

third_party_sharing:
- is_shared: true
  notes: >-
    The dataset is made available beyond the contributing centers under controlled access. The
    AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program is described as expanding access to
    Bridge2AI CHoRUS data; its Cohort 2, announced for November 17, 2025 through July 31, 2026, will
    select up to 30 trainees who work with the data on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care
    Collaborative Cloud after signing the licensing agreement.

existing_uses:
- examples:
  - As of August 2025, the datasets are being used for training activities and publications.
- examples:
  - >-
    Characterization reports are produced from site submissions and returned to the contributing
    sites (CHoRUSReports).

intended_uses:
- use_category: Clinical AI/ML model development
  examples:
  - Building machine learning and AI models to characterize acute and critical care illness
  - Predicting complications and deterioration in patients with acute or critical illness
  - Measuring treatment response
  usage_notes: >-
    The project's stated aim is to build ML- and AI-derived models that improve the care and
    outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
- use_category: External validation of clinical AI models
  examples:
  - Evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset
  usage_notes: >-
    Intended to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and
    critical care.
- use_category: Workforce training and AI literacy
  examples:
  - Hands-on trainee research on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud
  - Canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP common data model workshops and clinical deep learning exercises
  usage_notes: >-
    The project cultivates expertise in the lay and scientific community to improve AI literacy and
    utilization through multimodal educational approaches.

other_tasks:
- task_details: >-
    Analyses incorporating social determinants of health, which the project accounts for in its
    patient-focused ethical and legal work and harmonizes through its unified standards.

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The sequestered holdout set is intended to support external validation and thereby aid
    marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
- impact_details: >-
    Because the data derive from critically ill patients, the project frames privacy, accountability
    and clinical benefit as conditions on future use, with patient-focused work determining the
    ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants
    of health.
- impact_details: >-
    Community perspectives gathered through ethics focus groups determine what data is appropriate
    for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings.

maintainers:
- maintainer_details: >-
    Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, Massachusetts General Hospital, listed as the project contact on
    the CHoRUS website (cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, address as printed on the site).
  role: academic_institution
- maintainer_details: >-
    Access requests are handled by dbold@emory.edu and by Jared Houghtaling
    (jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org), listed as the contacts of the chorus-ai organization.
  role: academic_institution
- maintainer_details: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub organization maintains 28 repositories of CHoRUS software and documentation;
    versions, maintainers and other package metadata are tracked on a package status page, with
    contributor and user documentation compiled in the chorus-developer repository.
  role: other

updates:
  update_details: >-
    The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient
    admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025,
    de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata
    publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned.
  source_caveats: The bundle does not state an update frequency or a versioning policy.

extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai
  extension_details: >-
    Contributing sites submit regular status updates on their extraction and curation progress,
    either through the GitHub interface directly or through a Google Form whose submissions update
    GitHub status and issue information automatically; these statuses feed the Standards Project and
    the Data Acquisition Project. Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping through the
    chorus-mapping repository under a clinical validation SOP. Problems encountered in creating or
    submitting a data extract are posted in the Standards Discussions or Data Acquisition
    Discussions.

external_resources:
- external_resources:
  - >-
    CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/), with pages on the team, project overview, tools,
    data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai), 28 public repositories providing
    software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings, standard operating protocols
    for contributing sites, and project management overviews.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Chorus_SOP - centralized SOP documentation site with an interactive workflow diagram describing
    the step-by-step process for extracting and contributing clinical data to CHoRUS.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-mapping - documentation and pooled tabular mappings with an associated clinical validation
    SOP for contributing to mapping efforts.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources - waveform documentation, conversion scripts, and
    resources supporting the preparation and release of waveforms.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-extract-upload - tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract; chorus-container-apps -
    dockerized container applications and configurations deployed to support CHoRUS services on Azure.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    privacy_scan_tool - a privacy scan tool for medical records; CTP-deid; UF-Geocoding - open source
    code to geocode OMOP Location entities via DeGauss.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    CHoRUSReports - repository producing characterization reports returned to sites following their
    data submissions.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Bridge2AI project page for CHoRUS (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) and the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for
    Clinical Care training program call for applications hosted on AIM-AHEAD.net.

source_caveats: >-
  Four sources were used, ranked: the CHoRUS project website (project_documentation, tier 2), the
  NIH RePORTER project page for OT2OD032701 (tier 4), the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care
  Cohort 2 informational webinar of September 2025 (tier 4), and a 2025-11-14 capture of the
  chorus-ai GitHub organization overview (tier 5). The 2022 award abstract is written in the future
  tense about project plans and is recorded here as intention rather than as current dataset state.
  Volume figures differ between the tier-2 website (50,000 released admissions) and the tier-4
  webinar (over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025); the higher-ranked figure is stated with
  the disagreement noted at the affected instance. The webinar's imaging figure (1,000 images) and
  the website's (7,642 admissions with radiology data) count different units and are both retained.
  The 23 Tb waveform figure is reported for waveform data only, so no dataset-wide size is recorded.
  The cohort 2 webinar lists six people under the heading "Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team" with
  institutions but no individual role descriptions; only Eric Rosenthal is independently attested as
  principal investigator, by the NIH RePORTER project page, and principal_investigator is the only
  person-valued field the Creator class declares, so it carries each listed leader. The bundle
  states that CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and collaborates with the
  other three, but names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded.
